evidence_dispersion.rationale: The contract spans two structurally different React surfaces and the transport/scheduler boundary across two dependency hops.

contract_opacity.rationale: The prompt omits close invalidation and generation binding; the transport uses an unnamed boolean protocol and the adjacent consumer is a class rather than a reusable hook template.

temporal_composition.rationale: Correctness composes repeated polling, cancellation, stale-generation invalidation, exactly-once delivery, and scope preservation.

schedule_complexity.rationale: Four schedules vary repeated pending states, close timing, response status, and reopen generation.

consumer_heterogeneity.rationale: The foreground hook and background class encode two different ownership policies in different control structures.

repair_locus_ambiguity.rationale: Polling may be added to the foreground hook or moved toward the transport wrapper, while the class-based adjacent consumer cannot be copied mechanically.

framework_execution_complexity.rationale: The oracle mounts real React components and controls Promise completions, retry callbacks, close, reopen, and unmount boundaries.

structured_judgment.rationale: Structured events still require combining pending, close, generation, and ownership relations.

contract_recovery.rationale: Recovery must infer an unnamed status protocol, integrate structurally different consumers, and distinguish two ownership policies.

maintenance.rationale: The patch must restore polling and multiple invalidation obligations without globally applying dialog cancellation.
